source_refs.note: Topic 2.7.4, printed page 36: Hund's rule with the printed right and wrong arrangements.

blocks.text: Hund's rule says how to fill electrons into orbitals of equal energy, for example the three p orbitals px, py and pz. If three electrons are to be placed in three p orbitals there are two conceivable ways: all crowded into fewer orbitals with paired spins, or one in each orbital with the same spin. Hund's rule decides it.

blocks.title: Hund's rule
blocks.text: When degenerate orbitals are available and more than two electrons are to be placed in them, they should be placed in separate orbitals with the same spin rather than in the same orbital with opposite spins.
So the correct way to fill three electrons into three p orbitals is the one in which each orbital is singly occupied, with parallel spins.

blocks.prompt: Draw in words the orbital diagram of the 2p subshell of oxygen (four 2p electrons) and say which rule each feature obeys.
blocks.explanation: Three boxes px, py, pz. First one up arrow goes into each box, by Hund's rule, giving three parallel spins. The fourth electron must then pair, and it enters px with a down arrow, opposite to the one already there, by Pauli's principle. The result is one paired box and two singly occupied boxes.

items: Hund's rule: electrons entering degenerate orbitals occupy separate orbitals with the same spin before any pair up; three p electrons go one to each of px, py and pz.
